message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine the crime(s) from facts. Facts: defendant Stone (石某) went to hotel front desk, pretended to book a room, chatted, then at 11:50 he pretended to check in, asked staff Lin to go to workroom to get water, while Wang was at front desk, he stole cash of RMB 9400 placed at front desk and fled. So theft of cash from hotel. This is robbery? He used deception and took cash without violence? He used false pretenses to get access, but he didn't use force or threat, just took cash. That's theft (抢劫 requires violence or intimidation). He used deception to obtain cash, but still theft (盗窃). Could be "抢夺" but Chinese law: 盗窃罪 is taking property of others by stealth, etc. He used deception but not violence. So crime: theft (盗窃). Also maybe "诈骗" because he pretended to book room? But he didn't obtain money from victim by deception; he just stole cash. So only theft.

Thus answer: [罪名]盗窃<eoa>
